header.moduleTag: MODULE C • VECTORIZED JOINT AFFINITY ENGINE
header.title: Algorithmic Audience Curation & Propensity Engine
header.description: Replaces rigid boolean SQL filters with a multivariable demographic weighting matrix. Calculates joint cumulative affinity across all 14 businesses and cuts the top 5,000 households with the highest response probability.

math.title: Mathematical foundation of the propensity engine
math.individualFormula: score_i = Σ (w_ij × x_j)  for j = 1..7 attributes
math.individualNote: Dot product of the niche weight vector and the household's normalized demographic vector.
math.compositeNote: Cumulative joint affinity across all 14 businesses. The cut takes the 5,000 highest values.

comparison.eddm1: Routes bought by proximity or budget, without looking at who lives there.
comparison.eddm2: No way to tell the advertiser which neighbourhoods their ad landed in.
comparison.curation1: Every route in the ZIP is scored on USPS and Census data: income, ownership, housing type, vehicles, value and household size.
comparison.curation2: The best-scoring routes are bought until the target is covered, always whole.
comparison.curation3: The advertiser gets the route list and the neighbourhood profile, and can check it.

routeEngine.title: Route engine · who the drop reaches
routeEngine.intro: A co-op drop is delivered by saturation: the carrier leaves it in every box on the route, addressed to "Postal Customer". So the choice here is made by ROUTE, not by household, and no list has to be bought. USPS supplies each route's official box count; the Census supplies the profile of the households that route runs through. The ZIP's routes are scored on that, and the best ones are bought.
routeEngine.hybridNote: Each route is crossed with the Census block groups it runs through and weighted by households. Income and household size are published by USPS per route, but it leaves them empty in some ZIPs; when that happens the Census figure stands in and is tagged "ACS" so the origin is visible.
routeEngine.uspsOnlyNote: Scored on what USPS publishes per route. The Census enrichment did not answer this time; the weights renormalise themselves so routes stay comparable.

routeEngine.shortBody: Everything that leaves this screen — the pitch, the manifest, the neighbourhood profile — is presented as six variables. With one missing, the routes were ranked on a different basis than the one you will describe to the advertiser. Re-run the plan: it is nearly always the Census not answering, and it comes back on the second try. If you still need to continue, put it on the record.

census.why: Nothing was planned and nothing was saved. Four of the score's six variables come from the Census — income among them, at 35% — so without it you do not get a worse plan, you get a different product under the same name. Fix it and retry.
steps: Press Retry right here (nothing needs restarting)
